mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior to forecast
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS upshift (p > 0.05), or the 5-day forward return is positive despite the rate spike.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.3% for two consecutive months indicate a cooling inflationary trend, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts later in the quarter.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the next 60 days, the 20-day forward returns remain negative despite CPIAUCSL meeting the trigger, or the 60-day IC is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs in a single month coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive months of strong employment growth, the 5-day forward return remains negative or the 20-day IC is negative (>0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2.0% in a month signals weakening domestic demand, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as profit expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2.0% in a single month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive despite INDPRO meeting the trigger, or the 60-day IC is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in RSAFS (orders of magnitude) suggests softening demand for big-ticket durable goods, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower growth and tighter credit.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥10% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or RSAFS recovers sharply within 30 days, reversing the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (household spending) rises by more than 2% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer confidence and consumption momentum support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only in high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 250).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in UNRATE and a rise in PAYEMS by at least 50,000 jobs in the same month signals a transition from labor market weakness to strength, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market participants anticipate wage growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.00%), a sharp one-month drop in GDPC1 (GDP momentum) below 2% suggests a loss of momentum in economic activity, predicting a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion rises.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.00% AND GDPC1 falls by ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or GDPC1 recovers sharply within 30 days, invalidating the signal.
